paper.title: Algorithm 814: Fortran 90 software for floating-point multiple precision arithmetic, gamma and related functions (FM package, sample driver)
paper.note: DOI not verified in this wake; the article was not read (paywalled), so the claim rests on the shipped sample driver output Fortran90/Sp/Drivers/SAMPLE.CHK, sample 3.

code.note: Fortran 90 shar archive. Unpack the shar (remove everything above the #! /bin/sh line, run with /bin/sh) into a fresh directory; sources Fortran90/Sp/Src/FM.f90, FMSAVE.f90, FMZM90.f90 and the sample driver Fortran90/Sp/Drivers/SampleFM.f90. Compile with gfortran -O2 as the ReadMe describes and run SampleFM; its SAMPLE.LOG is compared with the shipped SAMPLE.CHK. Do not run inside the site directory.

claim.location: The shipped expected output SAMPLE.CHK, sample 3 (Zeta(3) by Gosper's series, computed in the FM package at 60 digits). The paper location was not read; no paper table or page is cited.
claim.metric: Riemann zeta(3) computed by Gosper's formula (5/4)*Sum[(-1)**k (k!)**2/((k+1)**2 (2k+1)!)] in the FM package at 60-digit precision (CALL FM_SET(60) in SampleFM.f90), compared with the printed digits.
claim.paper_value: Not used: the TOMS article was not read; the value is taken from the shipped expected output.

values.name: Zeta(3) (SAMPLE.CHK sample 3, 60-digit value rounded to double; first 16 significant digits 1.202056903159594)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The gate needs a numeric value, so the claim is the printed 60-digit Zeta(3) rounded to double precision, 1.2020569031595942 (true digits 1.20205690315959428539973816...; rounding error about 9e-17). Tolerance 1e-15 absorbs double-precision rounding of a correctly computed value. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 10 minutes: compile of FM90, FMSAVE and FMZM90 with gfortran -O2, then one short run.
cost.data_size: None; the sample driver generates its own inputs.
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence; the rerun should record the licence text.

why: A deterministic multiple-precision package whose shipped driver computes zeta(3), an irrational constant with no closed form here, so the run tests the 60-digit series arithmetic rather than a printed-by-hand value.
